teaser.en: Its flowers look torn in half, with all the petals on one side, as if someone had picked away the rest.

summary.en: Beach naupaka is a low succulent shrub of the beach crest and fore-dune, with fleshy leaves, half-flowers and black berries. It helps to hold the sand of Kenya's beaches in place.

about.en:
Beach naupaka is a low, spreading shrub with thick, fleshy leaves that resist the salt and sun of the beach. Its flowers are its most striking feature: the petals are all on one side, fanned out in a half-circle, so each flower looks like half a flower.

The flowers are followed by round berries that ripen black, which gives the plant its other English name, inkberry.

where.en: It grows on the fore-dune and beach crest of Kenya's sandy shores, the first band of shrubs above the open sand. Look for it in low mounds along the back of the beach, often with beach morning glory spreading at its feet.

uses.en: It is valued as a dune stabiliser: its roots and spreading stems hold the sand of the beach crest in place.

names.en: No Digo name has been recorded yet, and no Swahili name either. In English it is beach naupaka or inkberry, and its scientific name is *Scaevola plumieri*.
